key_insight: Machine-learning-driven molecular dynamics links aging in amorphous Ge₂Sb₂Te₅ to stronger axial-bond Peierls distortion, electronic band-gap widening, and reduced atomic mobility.
engineering_relevance: These structural insights may help explain aging-related resistance drift that compromises phase-change memory operation.
method: Use a machine-learning interatomic potential for molecular dynamics.
Simulate about 100 ns of aging after 24 ns of equilibration at 400 K.
Compute electronic band gaps with density functional theory in smaller aged amorphous models.
evidence_signal: The simulations show enhanced Peierls distortion, longer bond lifetimes, and lower atomic mobility during aging, while DFT calculations indicate band-gap widening.
watch_item: Homopolar bonds did not decrease within the simulated window; their removal may require much longer timescales.
paper_title: Brute-force molecular dynamics simulation of aging in amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$
